[0] According to the latest IDC report, although Mac shipments in Q3 2026 fell by 11%, Apple's market share actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5% because overall market shipments dropped sharply by 20.1%. Details are as follows.

[1] Despite a challenging environment, Apple still outperformed most of the PC market

[2] IDC today released its Q3 2026 global PC shipment report, noting that although Mac shipments fell year-on-year, Apple clearly outperformed the overall market.

[3] According to IDC's preliminary figures, Apple shipped a total of 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same quarter last year.

[4] However, the overall PC market declined even more sharply, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-on-year to 62.7 million units.

[5] As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

[6] Apple remains the world's fourth-largest PC manufacturer, behind Lenovo. Lenovo took the top spot with 14.9 million shipments and 23.8% market share; HP followed closely with 10.3 million shipments and 16.5% market share; Dell ranked third with 7.6 million shipments and 12.1% market share.

[7] Among the top five manufacturers, HP posted the largest year-on-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS had the smallest decline, down 8.6% year-on-year, with shipments of 5.5 million units and market share of 8.7%.

[9] Looking ahead, IDC mentioned that "with high inventory and elevated prices, channel concerns about weak demand could lead to more promotional activity in the near term," and added that "prices will remain well above historical levels."

[10] The firm also pointed out that the economy has weakened since the previous quarter, which may further suppress demand, making "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and 2027 even more dismal."
